title: Find XOR Sum of All Pairs Bitwise AND
statement:
You get two arrays of non-negative integers, `arr1` and `arr2`. For every way of choosing one index `i` of `arr1` and one index `j` of `arr2`, form the bitwise AND `arr1[i] & arr2[j]`; this gives `arr1.length * arr2.length` values in total.

Return the bitwise XOR of all of those values combined. (The XOR of a single value is that value itself.)
notes:
## Intuition

Listing every pair costs O(n · m), up to 10^10 operations. Bitwise AND distributes over XOR, the same way multiplication distributes over addition: `(a & b) ^ (a & c) = a & (b ^ c)`. So all the pairs that share `arr1[i]` collapse to `arr1[i] & (XOR of arr2)`, and doing the same over `i` collapses everything to `(XOR of arr1) & (XOR of arr2)`. Bit by bit: a bit is set in the answer when the number of pairs with that bit set in both values is odd, which happens exactly when an odd number of `arr1` values and an odd number of `arr2` values have it.

## Approach

1. XOR every value of `arr1` into `xor1`.
2. XOR every value of `arr2` into `xor2`.
3. Return `xor1 & xor2`.

## Example 1, step by step

`arr1 = [1, 2, 3]`: `xor1` goes 0 → 1 → 3 → 0.
`arr2 = [6, 5]`: `xor2` goes 0 → 6 → 3.
The answer is `0 & 3 = 0`, matching the six pair values `[0, 1, 2, 0, 2, 1]` whose XOR is `0`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + m): each array is scanned once.
- Space: O(1): two running XOR values.

## Pitfalls

- Do not build the list of pairs; it has up to 10^10 entries.
- XOR is not addition: the identity is `a & (b ^ c)`, and it does not hold if you swap the roles of AND and XOR.
- Start both accumulators at `0`, the neutral value for XOR (starting at `arr1[0]` and then XORing it again cancels it).

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `xor1` | XOR of all values in `arr1` |
| `xor2` | XOR of all values in `arr2` |
| `value` | the array element being folded in |

narration.2: Start the XOR of arr1 at 0, which leaves any value unchanged.
narration.4: Fold it into the running XOR; each bit flips once per value that has it.
narration.7: Start the XOR of arr2 the same way.
narration.9: Fold it into the second running XOR.
narration.12: AND distributes over XOR, so all the pair ANDs XORed together equal xor1 & xor2.
